title: How to File Form 5472 and 1120 as a Non-US Resident Running a Single-Member LLC in 2026
content:
# How to File Form 5472 and 1120 as a Non-US Resident Running a Single-Member LLC in 2026

If you're a non-US resident running a single-member LLC in the United States, you have a specific tax filing obligation that catches many foreign entrepreneurs off guard: filing Form 5472 alongside a pro forma Form 1120 every single year, even if your LLC earned zero dollars.

---

## Why This Filing Requirement Exists

The IRS treats a foreign-owned single-member LLC as a disregarded entity, but it still classifies it as a corporation for information reporting purposes. That distinction is everything.

Because of this classification, your LLC must file:

- **Form 5472:** Reports transactions between your LLC and its foreign owner (you)
- **Pro forma Form 1120:** A stripped-down corporate return that acts as a "jacket" for Form 5472

This is purely a reporting requirement, not an income tax filing. You are not paying US income tax through this process unless your LLC has effectively connected income, which is a separate topic entirely.

---

## Who Must File

You must file Form 5472 and the pro forma 1120 if all of the following apply:

- You are not a US citizen or permanent resident
- You own 100% of a US single-member LLC
- Your LLC engaged in any "reportable transaction" during the tax year

Reportable transactions are broader than most people expect. They include capital contributions, distributions, loans between you and the LLC, payments for services, and even formation costs you paid on behalf of the company.

> **Note:** "No income" does not mean "no filing." If you contributed startup capital or paid any LLC expenses personally, that is already a reportable transaction. Missing this filing carries a minimum penalty of $25,000 per violation.

---

## The Filing Deadline

The deadline mirrors the corporate tax calendar:

- **Due date:** April 15 of the year following the tax year
- **Extension available:** File Form 7004 to extend to October 15
- **Tax year:** Calendar year (January 1 to December 31) for most single-member LLCs

If your LLC was formed mid-year, your first filing covers from the date of formation through December 31 of that same year.

---

## What Goes on the Pro Forma 1120

The pro forma 1120 is not a full corporate tax return. You only need to complete a minimal version of it. Here is exactly what to include:

1. **Header section:** LLC name, address, and EIN
2. **Box for tax year:** Check "Other" and write in your LLC's tax year dates
3. **Attach Form 5472:** Staple or attach it directly to the 1120
4. Write "Foreign-Owned U.S. DE" at the top of the 1120

Leave all income, deduction, and balance sheet sections completely blank. This form exists only to give the IRS a corporate return framework to attach the 5472 to.

---

## What Goes on Form 5472

Form 5472 has several parts. For most foreign-owned single-member LLCs, you will use:

- **Part I:** LLC information (name, EIN, country of incorporation of owner)
- **Part II:** Foreign owner's information (your name, address, country of residence)
- **Part IV:** Monetary transactions (contributions, distributions, payments)
- **Part VI:** Nonmonetary transactions (property transfers, if applicable)

Be precise with dollar amounts. Round to the nearest dollar and use the exchange rate on the transaction date for any amounts originally in a foreign currency.

> **Note:** If you have multiple transaction types across Part IV and Part VI, list each category separately. Do not lump everything into one line.

---

## How to Submit the Filing

This is where many people get tripped up. You cannot e-file this particular combination.

**Mail your package to:**

Internal Revenue Service
1973 Rulon White Blvd.
Ogden, UT 84201

Send it via certified mail or an international courier with tracking. Keep your proof of delivery permanently. The IRS has been known to misplace mailed filings, and your proof of postmark is your legal protection.

---

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

| Mistake | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Filing late or not at all | Minimum $25,000 penalty per year |
| Missing transactions in Part IV | Potential audit and additional penalties |
| Forgetting the pro forma 1120 | Return considered incomplete |
| Using the wrong address | Filing lost, deadline missed |
| Omitting the "Foreign-Owned U.S. DE" label | Processing delays |

---

## Do You Need a US Tax Professional?

For straightforward situations, many foreign LLC owners handle this filing themselves once they understand the structure. If any of the following apply to you, professional help is worth the cost:

- Your LLC has actual US-source income
- You have multiple LLCs or a more complex ownership structure
- You are unsure whether specific transactions are reportable
- You missed a prior year's filing and need to file late
